must_fix.issue: The line 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements with you before you travel, as these rules can change.' sits at the end of the customs section, where it reads as an upsell or as addressed to an existing client. Raised by 4 of 5 personas (funding_parent medium, planner_couple medium as primary persona, search_visitor, sceptic).
must_fix.fix: Remove it from 'Declaring it on return to Australia' and end that section on a neutral line, e.g. 'These rules can change, so check the Australian Border Force page before you travel.' (the ABF link is already in the section; do not add a second link). Keep the Wedded Advisor line, but move it to the closing 'From the ring to the destination' section, directly after the Wedded Concierge sentence, framed for Concierge couples, e.g. 'If you plan with Wedded Concierge, your Wedded Advisor confirms the current customs requirements with you before you travel, as these rules can change.' That position also explains who the Advisor is the first time a newcomer meets them.

should_fix.issue: Key takeaway 4 (AUD900 duty-free allowance) spends one of four first-screen slots on a niche Australian customs rule; it sets a mass-market tone and ignores natural vs lab-grown, the question readers wanted answered up top.
should_fix.fix: Replace takeaway 4 with one sentence on natural vs lab-grown, drawn only from facts already in the draft (FAQ: essentially the same optical, physical and chemical properties; checklist: origin confirmed in writing on receipt and report), e.g. 'Lab-grown and natural diamonds look and behave essentially the same, so get natural or lab-grown confirmed in writing on both the receipt and the report.' Keep exactly 4 takeaways, one sentence each. The AUD900 detail stays in the travel section and FAQ unchanged.

should_fix.issue: The closing Wedded Concierge sentence ('plans venue, travel, vendors and payments ... single point of contact') is a promise with nothing behind it; 'payments' raises the money question without any reassurance.
should_fix.fix: Add one plain sentence using only brand-facts claims: the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and the Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. Do not state a fee model, commission position, deposit protection or any price; these are deferred business items (see conflicts_resolved). No prices.

consider.issue: 'This diamond buying guide has nothing to sell in the stone itself.' reads as a lawyer's hedge ('what's the catch?').
consider.fix: brand-facts.md does not state that Wedded Wonderland sells no diamonds (and Wedded Marketplace is a vendor directory), so do not replace it with a 'we sell no diamonds' claim. Cut the hedge sentence and let the opening line carry the point: 'Most advice on choosing a diamond is written by someone with a tray of stones to sell you. This guide ranks the 4Cs by ...'.

consider.issue: Fluorescence statistics (25% to 35%, more than 95% blue, fewer than 0.2%) slow the section; readers want the practical point.
consider.fix: Trim to the practical takeaway: fluorescence rarely affects how a stone looks, it does not cause haziness on its own, blue can help in I to M stones, and view a fluorescent stone in daylight beside stones of the same grade. Keep the GIA link and fact markers on whatever survives; drop the percentage figures from the body (they can stay out entirely).

consider.issue: The shortlist checklist is the most shareable block but is hard to find on mobile.
consider.fix: Turn 'A shortlist checklist sits near the end.' in the intro into a jump link to the '## Your diamond shortlist checklist' heading anchor.

consider.issue: Readers want a price steer next to the takeaways.
consider.fix: No prices. Move or repeat the existing budget link so it sits directly after the Key takeaways list, e.g. 'For the money side, see our guide on how much to spend on an engagement ring.' using /expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring. Link it once only; if moved up, remove the later duplicate in the 4Cs section.

consider.issue: Tone: 'This takes two minutes.' and 'workable with a little paperwork' read slightly eager and understate what carrying a significant stone involves.
consider.fix: Cut 'This takes two minutes.' Reword 'workable with a little paperwork' to something like 'is straightforward with the right paperwork and insurance in place.' No new security or courier claims.

consider.issue: 'This guide does not rank them' (GIA vs IGI) reads as a dodge.
consider.fix: Only if the source pack holds a sourced comparison, add it. Otherwise one plain clause that we found no independent published comparison we could cite. Do not invent one.

keep: Opening line: 'Most advice on choosing a diamond is written by someone with a tray of stones to sell you.' (praised by all five personas)
'Our view is simple. For a round brilliant, put cut first.' and the cut-first takeaway
Report check: 'Type the number in yourself, on the lab's own website, rather than following a link or QR code someone hands you' and 'before any money moves'
'A report is not a valuation' section
Kimberley Process honesty: 'speaks to one specific problem'
'We found no Australian guidance written specifically for lab-grown diamonds' (admitting gaps builds trust)
Customs detail in the travel section: duty applies to all goods of that type, declare with proof of purchase, penalties stated plainly
Insurance and hand luggage guidance, copies kept separately from the ring
Low-pressure closing CTA placed after the evidence, destinations hub first
conflicts_resolved: 'Nothing to sell in the stone itself': funding_parent took it as reassurance, sceptic as a hedge. The reassurance comes from the opening line, which every persona praised; the qualifier adds suspicion only. Cut the qualifier, keep the opening line. A plain 'we sell no diamonds' line is not supported by brand-facts.md, so it is not added.

Fee model, supplier commissions, deposit protection, a named Advisor or phone line, real weddings with venue and date, a private or referral route, scale (200 to 400 guests) and secure jewellery transport were requested by sceptic, funding_parent, planner_couple and uhnw. All are deferred business items in brand-facts.md, so none is a must-fix and none may be invented. Addressed only with existing brand-facts claims (fee and inclusions agreed in writing). Logged for the business to answer.

Customs content: search_visitor (non-Australian) wanted it gone; planner_couple (primary) and funding_parent valued the plain customs detail. The brief explicitly includes carrying the stone through customs for Australian couples, so it stays in full in the travel section and FAQ and only leaves the takeaways.

Depth: uhnw (relevance 1) found the guide too basic; planner_couple and search_visitor found it useful. The brief targets the planner_couple reader at the dreaming stage, so the depth stays; uhnw's tone notes are taken as light copy changes only.

Low weighted enquiry likelihood (1.7) is expected for a dreaming-stage diamond guide whose primary goal is a click to /destinations, not an enquiry. Gate stays revise per the rule; the fixes above improve trust around the CTA but are not expected to lift enquiry likelihood to 3.8. Do not add sales copy to chase the score.
